{{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Jinja
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Jinja | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]] | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Jinja'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Jinja'''|国府宮神社|}} or the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''Kokuhei Shōsha''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{commons category-inline|Owari Okunitama-jinja}} *[http://www.konomiya.or.jp Official website] {{Shinto shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Owari Province]] [[Category:Inazawa, Aichi]] [[Category:Soja]]

It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons 尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry
