{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Inazawa, Aichi}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Owari Ōkunitama Shrine
尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. 尾張大国霊神社 | image = Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|15|22|N|136|48|18.5|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama Okami|lt=Okunitama|simple|Kunitama Omikami|ja|国魂|12=draft}} | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category-inline|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine}} *[http://www.konomiya.or.jp Official website] {{Shinto shrine}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{draft categories| [[Category:11]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:Pages that used to use Authority control]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Owari Province]] [[Category:Inazawa]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Kokuhei Shōsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Prefecturally designated intangible folk cultural property]] [[Category:Owari-zukuri]] [[Category:1 revision imported]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]][[Category:qq]] }} [[en:Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]] [[sn:Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]]

It was the ''[[Sōja (Shinto)|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was Ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd Rank {{nihongo|''[[kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. [[:en:Kunitama|Okunitama]] | founded_by = | established = pre-[[Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja shrine|sōja]]'' of [[Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was Ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd Rank {{nihongo|''[[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[Rōmon]]'', built in early [[Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category-inline|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine}} *[http://www.konomiya.or.jp Official website] {{Shinto shrine}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Owari Province]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Kokuhei Shōsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Prefecturally designated intangible folk cultural property]] [[Category:Owari-zukuri]] }} [[sn:Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]] [[en:Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Pages with valid en interwikis]] [[Category:pages with valid en interwikis 2]] {{Commons category|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine}} [[ja:尾張大国霊神社]] [[zh:尾張大國靈神社]]

尾張大国霊神社 | image = File:Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{Coord|35.25611111111111|N|136.8051388888889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
[[:en:Kunitama|Okunitama]] | founded_by = | established = pre-[[:en:Nara period|Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = | prefecture= {{ill|Inazawa|WD=Q389562}} }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[:en:Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja shrine|sōja]]'' of [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was Ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd Rank {{nihongo|''[[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[:en:Rōmon|Rōmon]]'', built in early [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[:en:List of Shinto shrines|List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category-inline|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine}} *[http://www.konomiya.or.jp Official website] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Owari Province]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Kokuhei Shōsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Prefecturally designated intangible folk cultural property]] [[Category:Owari-zukuri]] }} [[en:Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] {{Commons category|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine}} [[ja:尾張大国霊神社]] [[zh:尾張大國靈神社]] {{wikidata link|Q11465296}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]]

[[:en:Kunitama|Okunitama]] | founded_by = | established = pre-[[:en:Nara period|Nara period]] | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = | prefecture= {{ill|Inazawa|WD=Q389562}} }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the city of [[:en:Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It was the ''[[Sōja shrine|sōja]]'' of [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]]. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]] [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was Ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd Rank {{nihongo|''[[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]: * ''[[:en:Rōmon|Rōmon]]'', built in early [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *[[:en:List of Shinto shrines|List of Shinto shrines]] * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category-inline|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine}} *[http://www.konomiya.or.jp Official website] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Sōja shrines}} [[en:Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]] {{Commons category|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine}} [[ja:尾張大国霊神社]] [[zh:尾張大國靈神社]] {{wikidata link|Q11465296}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kokuhei Shōsha]] [[Category:Owari Province]] [[Category:Owari-zukuri]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Prefecturally designated intangible folk cultural property]] [[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

尾張大国霊神社 | image = File:Kounomiya1.JPG | caption = ''Heiden'' of Owari Ōkunitama Shrine | map_type = Japan Aichi Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{Coord|35.25611111111111|N|136.8051388888889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Ōkuninushi]]
{{ill|Kunitama|en|Kunitama|WD=Q9692242|lt=Okunitama|1=Kunitama}} | founded_by = | established = pre-{{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|WD=Q189178|lt=Nara period|1=Nara period}} | date_destroyed = | location = Inazawa-shi, Aichi-ken | website = {{Official website|1=http://www.konomiya.or.jp}} | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = | prefecture= {{ill|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|1=Inazawa}} }} {{nihongo|'''Owari Ōkunitama Shrine'''|尾張大国霊神社|Owari Ōkunitama Jinja}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in the city of [[:en:Inazawa, Aichi|Inazawa]], {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}. It was the ''[[Sōja shrine|sōja]]'' of {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}}. The main ''[[kami]]'' enshrined is [[Ōkuninushi]]. The shrine's main festival is held annually on May 6. Due to its location near the site of the {{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|WD=Q189178|lt=Nara period|1=Nara period}} [[kokufu|provincial capital]] of Owari Province, it is also called the {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya Shrine'''|国府宮神社|}} or {{nihongo|'''Kōnomiya'''|国府宮|}} ==History== The original construction of this shrine is unknown. Although nominally dedicated to Ōkuninushi, this affiliation is uncertain, and the shrine asserts that it is dedicated to the tutelary spirits of the ancestors of the people of Owari. It became the ''sōja'' of Owari during the Nara period, and is mentioned in the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}} ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the pre-World War II [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was Ranked as a National Shrine, 3rd Rank {{nihongo|''[[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|}}. Two of the shrine's structures have been designated national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Properties|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}: * ''{{ill|Rōmon|en|Rōmon|WD=Q3458957|lt=Rōmon|1=Rōmon}}'', built in early {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|WD=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period|1=Muromachi period}}{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/146461 |title=尾張大国霊神社楼門 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} * [[Heiden (Shinto)|''Heiden'']], built in the early {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/174502 |title=尾張大国霊神社拝殿 |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}} File:Konomiya2.JPG|Torii and entry File:Konomiya3.JPG|Gate (ICP) File:Kounomiya-hadakamaturi.jpg|Hadaka Matsuri ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|en|List of Shinto shrines|WD=Q120679573|lt=List of Shinto shrines|1=List of Shinto shrines}} * [[Kunitama]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category-inline|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine}} *[http://www.konomiya.or.jp Official website] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Sōja shrines}} [[en:Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]] {{Commons category|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine}} [[ja:尾張大国霊神社]] [[zh:尾張大國靈神社]] {{wikidata link|Q11465296}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kokuhei Shōsha]] [[Category:Owari Province]] [[Category:Owari-zukuri]] [[Category:Prefecturally designated intangible folk cultural property]] [[Category:Shikinai Shōsha]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Shikinai Shōsha]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]]
